label: Yards needed
description: The yardage the play has to gain to count as a success: 40% of the distance to the sticks on 1st down, 60% on 2nd, all of it on 3rd and 4th.

label: Receiver depth
description: Where the receiver is relative to the line of scrimmage, in yards. Negative values mean the receiver is still behind it.

label: Extra room ahead
description: How much further away the nearest defender in front of the receiver is than the receiver's closest defender. Zero when the closest defender is the one in front.

label: Closest defender across the field
description: Smallest sideline-to-sideline gap between the receiver and any defender.

label: Nearest defender's cushion
description: How far downfield of the receiver the nearest defender is. Negative values mean the defender is trailing the receiver.

label: Defensive width
description: How spread out the defenders are across the field (standard deviation).

label: Closing speed of the nearest three
description: Average closing speed of the three defenders closest to the receiver.

label: Nearest defender's distance from a blocker
description: Distance from the closest defender to the nearest offensive player (which may be the quarterback). Larger values mean nobody is near enough to block that defender.

label: Relative speed of the defender and nearest offensive player
description: How fast the closest defender and their nearest offensive player are moving relative to each other. Larger values mean their velocities differ more; they could be approaching or moving apart or across one another.
